text: Working with APIs is a common task for developers. An API lets your program communicate with another service, usually through HTTP requests. When you send a request, the server often responds with data in JSON format. Before you can access the data, you usually need authentication, such as an API key. Many services also have rate limits, which means you can only make a certain number of requests per minute or hour. Finally, good error handling is important. If something goes wrong, the API may return an error code, and your program should handle it properly without crashing.
